seo.title: Woven vs Printed Labels: Which Fits Your Garment?
seo.description: Compare woven and printed labels for logo detail, comfort, washing, and total cost, with sample checks and a practical buyer specification.

title: Woven vs Printed Labels: Which Fits Your Garment?
lead: Woven labels build your design from yarn; printed labels apply it to an existing material. Choose woven for textured branding and printed for intricate artwork or dense care information, then judge the actual sewn sample. See [Cruz Label’s artwork comparison](https://cruzlabel.com/blogs/clothing-label-blog/woven-vs-printed-labels-what-will-work-best-for-my-artwork).
At Tapa Works, we offer woven branding, printed neck labels, and care and size labels. You can combine techniques across the garment; see our [Custom Labels & Hang Tags](/custom-labels-hang-tags/).

sections.heading: Woven and printed labels compared: detail, feel, durability, and cost

body.text: Choose woven labels when you want textured branding, or printed labels for fine artwork or dense information; printed labels often cost less. Comfort, wash performance and delivered cost depend on how the finished label is made, so compare sewn samples and complete quotes. See [Quality Woven Labels? Woven Labels vs Printed Labels: How to Choose the Right One](https://qualitywovenlabels.com/blog/post/woven-labels-vs-printed-labels-how-to-choose-the-right-one).

body.text: To see artwork examples that illustrate these tradeoffs, visit [Cruz Label’s Woven vs Printed Labels. What will work best for my artwork?](https://cruzlabel.com/blogs/clothing-label-blog/woven-vs-printed-labels-what-will-work-best-for-my-artwork). Ask about color limits and request an actual-size proof for the proposed construction.

For our leaf-logo comparison, we used matching 40 × 20 mm polyester damask and screen-printed polyester satin labels. Both kept letters readable at 1.5 mm high, but the woven 0.2 mm leaf veins merged while the printed veins stayed separate. We widened the woven veins to 0.4 mm and changed the gradient to solid colors. The finished sample kept those revised lines intact.

In our shared cotton-poplin neck-label comparison, both sewn end-fold samples remained readable after laundering. The woven label had slight corner curl but no visible fading; the printed label stayed flat, though its pale veins lightened. Neither frayed or lost stitches. Wearers noticed the exposed woven corner more often, and tucking it under the seam reduced rubbing. The next section covers the wash routine, specimen results and thickness measurements. When approving your sample, check artwork, edges and attachment separately in the same way.

For an assumed order of 500 usable labeled garments with matching artwork, dimensions, folds and no added variants, budget USD 150 for woven labels or USD 100 for printed labels. Setup is USD 40 or USD 20, freight to the US is USD 30 either way, and application is USD 50 either way. Add our USD 50 garment sample, USD 50 design fee and USD 50 sample courier charge to each option. That brings the totals to USD 420 woven and USD 350 printed: USD 0.84 and USD 0.70 per usable garment. Label, setup, freight and application costs are assumed inputs, not our rates. Our sample, design and courier fees are nonrefundable and are not credited to bulk.

chart.caption: Assumed total cost including sampling and application

body.text: For our woven labels, allow 3–5 days for design and proofing and 7–15 days for label sampling alongside shirt sampling; bulk labels follow the shirt schedule. Request dated quotes that list proof approval, production and US transit separately. Before comparing total cost, choose the sample that keeps your essential artwork intact and passes your garment’s comfort and care checks.

A woven label is a fabric tag with lettering and a logo made from threads interlaced on a loom, so the design becomes part of the fabric. Damask supports fine detail and durable branding, with flat or folded finishes for sewing. See [Dutch Label Shop’s Custom Woven Labels Made to Last](https://www.dutchlabelshop.com/en_us/woven-labels/).

For our leaf-logo walkthrough, we used matching 40 × 20 mm polyester damask and screen-printed polyester satin samples. The original artwork included a gradient and fine veins; in the digitized woven proof, we replaced the gradient with solid yarn colors and widened the veins. On the woven front, the revised veins stayed separate and the lettering remained readable. On the reverse, you could trace the motif through the yarn paths. The printed sample kept the original fine veins. Compare your proof with the actual fabric at finished size, then turn it over to check the construction.

For the shared wash comparison, we sewed end-fold samples at matching neck positions on cotton poplin. We ran 10 normal washes at 40°C with unscented liquid detergent, no bleach, and line drying. In daylight, we compared the dry samples with unwashed controls, reading them at arm’s length and checking edges and stitches under a magnifier.

rows: Revised lettering readable; no visible fading

body.text: Before approval, record how the artwork, edges and attachment each hold up under your garment’s intended care routine.

Our folded woven edge measured 0.6 mm thick; printed satin measured 0.4 mm. During seated adult wear checks before and after laundering, we asked wearers to identify contact from the face, edge, fold and stitching separately. Wearers reported more rubbing from the exposed woven corner; tucking it under the seam reduced those reports. Preferences for the label face were mixed.

Turn your sewn sample inside out to check it, then wear it normally. Note exactly where it touches your neck and repeat the check after washing. Choose the weave to suit your artwork, then use the fold and placement checks below to decide how it sits on the garment.

sections.heading: What are the different types of woven labels?

body.text: Damask, satin, and taffeta are the main woven-label constructions. Damask suits fine detail, satin offers a smooth, lustrous face, and taffeta suits simpler, economical designs. Choose the weave for your artwork, then the fold for where the label will sit. See [Etiketi’s Woven Label Manufacturer – Damask & Satin](https://etiketi.eu/collections/woven-labels).

Keep the specifications separate: cotton names a fiber, HD is a grade you need to verify with samples, selvage means a woven edge, and center-fold describes an installation shape. Along with the sample, ask for yarn fineness, weave density, edge finish, and a folded-size drawing.

Our leaf-logo strip compared standard damask, HD damask, satin, and taffeta in matching polyester colors at 40 × 20 mm. HD kept the smallest letter openings clearer than standard damask, but neither preserved the original hairline veins. Satin blurred those openings, and taffeta lost the most detail. The revised bold leaf remained recognizable across the strip.

In our cotton-poplin placement check, hot-cut polyester damask with end folds rubbed at an exposed neck corner both before and after the care routine above. We also checked the same weave and edge finish center-folded into a side seam, with the cut ends enclosed. Wearers reported less rubbing, although they could feel the seam bulk. Neither sample frayed, and comfort feedback favored the enclosed edges.

Use this worksheet to compare the proposed installation with the maker’s drawing. For fold terminology, see [Quality Woven Labels’ Woven Labels vs Printed Labels: How to Choose](https://qualitywovenlabels.com/blog/post/woven-labels-vs-printed-labels-how-to-choose-the-right-one) and [Etiketi’s Woven Label Manufacturer – Damask & Satin](https://etiketi.eu/collections/woven-labels).

body.text: If you start with a 2-inch (50.8 mm) flat strip and allow 0.25-inch (6.35 mm) end turnbacks, the folded face is 1.5 inches (38.1 mm) long before stitching clearance. Mark the visible artwork, hidden turnbacks, and stitch lines separately.

figure.caption: Tucked ends leave the center face visible

body.text: Approve the sewn sample where you intend to place it, then check the edges and bulk again after garment care. Check logo clarity and installation comfort separately.

sections.heading: What material are woven labels made of?

body.text: Woven labels commonly use polyester yarn, though cotton is another option. See [Weavabel's Printed vs Woven Labels: Which Should You Choose?](https://www.weavabel.com/blog/printed-labels-vs-woven-labels-which-are-better).

Damask, satin, and taffeta describe constructions, while cotton-look polyester is still polyester. See [Etiketi's Woven Label Manufacturer – Damask & Satin](https://etiketi.eu/collections/woven-labels).

Our leaf-logo damask had polyester ground and design yarns, hot-cut edges, and no coating, softener, or adhesive. Its recycled status was unverified. For the recycled trial, supplier records covered the plain ground and logo yarns, but the claim did not cover metallic yarns or the heat-seal backing.

We compared the faces of our matching polyester leaf samples by bending and rubbing them between our fingertips, then checked exposed edges on sewn cotton poplin. Satin felt smoother but blurred small letter openings; HD damask kept them clearer. Without changing the damask yarn or density, we reduced edge contact by enclosing the hot-cut ends.

We extended the cotton-poplin wash routine above to matched virgin and documented recycled damask. The heat-seal samples had a polyurethane backing applied at 150°C for 15 seconds at 3 bar; the sewn samples had no backing. We measured the dry labels and compared them with unwashed controls.

body.text: In your specification, list ground yarn, design yarn, finish, and backing separately. Make sure the recycled documentation matches your selected colors and components. Ask for yarn fineness, density, and a sewn sample, then check readability and attachment separately after garment care.
Before you order, we confirm which certificates cover your selected trims and provide current copies on request. See our [Quality Control](/quality-control/).

sections.heading: Choose woven or printed labels from a finished sample

body.text: Base your choice on the artwork at actual size, comfort once sewn in, intended garment care, and the full delivered-and-applied quote. Send us your logo, finished dimensions, garment fabric, placement, fold, attachment, care routine, quantities, variants, US delivery address, and required arrival date.

We quote before sampling and start bulk production after you approve the sample. See our [Sampling](/sampling/) process, then use our [Request a Quote](/request-a-quote/) page to tell us about the label and garment together.
